Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up - Acme Retail

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and next steps. Please correct anything I missed.

What we heard during the call:
- Primary use case: customer-facing chat + assist for product search and summarization across user sessions.
- Preferred deployment mode: leaning to Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for predictable latency and data isolation; Private/VPC is a secondary option if compliance requires it.
- Peak targets: ~120 TPS (requests/sec) at peak hour, with average concurrency of 45 active sessions.
- Token mix: average prompt 250 tokens, average generated tokens 200, so ~450 tokens per request. Burst spikes up to ~700 tokens/request during heavier summaries.
- SLOs: 95th percentile latency target < 400ms for short prompts; acceptable fallbacks to smaller model for heavy requests.
- Security: SOC2 + customer-managed KMS are required.

Immediate asks from Acme:
1) Guidance on GPU type and counts for Dedicated (A100 vs H100 recommendation).
2) Estimated throughput per-GPU given token mix and concurrency.
3) Cost ballpark and next steps to run a short PoC / sizing test.

Next steps (from Redwood):
- I attached our Dedicated sizing template (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) — can you fill the expected request distribution and any additional workloads?
- Rafael (cc'd) will propose a recommended config (GPU type, node counts, expected TPS) by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review sizing and options (Dedicated vs Private).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (spreadsheet with worksheet tabs: workload_profile, token_mix, traffic_pattern)

Thanks — looking forward to your inputs.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 120 TPS is for short interactive queries (search/autocomplete). For long summaries the expected concurrent long-running requests are ~8–10 at peak.
- Token mix: the 450 tokens average you noted is correct for typical mix; long summaries can reach 1k tokens occasionally (1–2% of traffic).
- Compliance: we will need customer-managed KMS and access to audit logs for 365 days. Private/VPC is a hard requirement only if Dedicated cannot meet our encryption-at-rest and key management controls.

Questions for Rafael: given the above, what would you recommend for GPU type? We're trying to balance cost vs latency — is H100 materially better for our workload than an A100 80GB? Also, what concurrency per-GPU can we reasonably expect for the model you recommended on the call?

Happy to hop on the follow-up next week — prefer Tues/Wed morning PT.

Best,
Sarah

Marissa / Aditya —

Reviewing the notes and Sarah's clarifications. Initial recommendation (high level):

Model assumption: medium-sized open model with good latency/quality tradeoff (similar to Llama-2-13B-opt). If Acme chooses a larger LLM, numbers will change.

GPU recommendation: H100 provides better fp16/quantization throughput and will reduce latency for long-token requests. For your token mix (avg 450 tokens/request, spikes to 1k):
- 1x H100 (supernode) can handle ~60–70 short-requests TPS at ~350–450ms p95 for the above model with concurrency tuned.
- 1x A100 80GB can handle ~40–50 TPS at ~400–550ms p95, and will struggle more on 1k-token summaries.

Sizing for 120 TPS peak:
- Option A (latency-focused): 2 x H100 nodes (allowing a buffer for autoscale + maintenance). Expected aggregated steady TPS ~140 with headroom. Concurrency per-node tuned for ~24–30 active sessions.
- Option B (cost-balanced): 3 x A100 80GB nodes. Aggregated steady TPS ~130 but p95 latency will be higher on long summaries.

Other notes:
- Use prefix/KV caching for chat sessions to reduce repeated prompt cost; we can offset ~15–25% token compute for repetitive prompts.
- For PoC: propose a 2-week dedicated trial on 1 H100 node with synthetic replay of your peak-hour traffic (we can work with the sizing template to generate a replay).

I'll prepare a simple per-month cost delta for Option A vs Option B and include operational notes (autoscale policies, fallback to smaller variant). Will have that by EOD tomorrow.

Rafael
